title: Beatrix and the Crown
premise: Odile Brightwater has spent her life hiding her gift for speaking with beasts inside the Valley of Stillwater, where magic is smothered like a candle under a jar. When prayers to the old gods begin echoing off the valley's stones and her brother's soul is claimed by the court beneath the mountain as payment for a bargain their grandmother made, Odile must cross into the wild country where her gift is both salvation and a death sentence. Guided by a scarred wolf who remembers her grandmother, she bargains with river-spirits, outwits a god who collects debts in memory, and discovers the thirteenth moon is a door only she can open. At the climax she offers her own memories of her brother in exchange for his soul, but the wolf sacrifices his accumulated centuries to keep her whole; Odile returns home changed, carrying the valley's first true magic, and chooses truth over the invisibility that once kept her safe.
about_author: Hazel Iversen is the pen name of a former folklorist who spent a decade recording oral tales in remote mountain communities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasies about quiet people and loud magic from a farmhouse full of rescued animals who, she insists, answer back.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet her secretly comforting a lame ewe with her forbidden gift, establishing the valley's magic-dead silence and her family's careful invisibility. When a prayer she mutters over the ewe is answered by something ancient, the ground trembles. Emotional beat: the uneasy comfort of hiding shattered by a first crack of wonder.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons on the Doorpost
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her grandmother's death-day ritual reveals a hidden ledger: a bargain struck generations ago, one soul owed to the court beneath the mountain, due when the thirteenth moon completes its turn. That night, her brother Tam sleepwalks toward the treeline, eyes silver. Emotional beat: dread as family history becomes a ticking clock.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembered
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A scarred wolf appears at the valley's edge—impossible here—and speaks her grandmother's name. He claims to have known her, and warns that Tam's soul is already being weighed. The valley elders refuse to hear her warnings. Emotional beat: loneliness answered by an unlikely, wary alliance.

chapters.title: Leaving Stillwater
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile steals her grandmother's ledger, a bone whistle, and Tam's baby blanket as an anchor to his soul, and crosses the valley boundary at dawn. The moment she passes the stones, magic floods her senses—overwhelming, glorious, terrifying. Emotional beat: exhilaration and grief in leaving the only safe place she's known.

chapters.title: The River That Takes Toll
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the Graywater crossing, a river-spirit demands a toll of true memory. Odile pays the taste of her mother's bread, and in return learns the court beneath the mountain trades in souls and names. The wolf, called Ashen, teaches her to shield her gift. Emotional beat: first lesson that survival has a price paid in the self.

chapters.title: Beasts of the Burnt Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Traveling a war-scarred road, Odile speaks with crows who trade gossip for shin-bones, learning the old gods are waking because prayers have grown desperate enough to reach them. She is spotted by a tithe-collector—a hollow-eyed servant of the court—and barely escapes. Emotional beat: her gift shifts from shame to weapon.

chapters.title: The God of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a market town, a minor god of debts and thresholds corners Odile, offering to locate Tam's soul for the price of her name. Ashen intervenes, owing the god an old favor, buying her free but deepening their entanglement. Emotional beat: the realization that every helper in this world keeps a ledger too.

chapters.title: Ashen's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. Flashback chapters within his narration: he was her grandmother's companion, bound to witness the original bargain and forbidden to intervene until a Brightwater freely asked. He confesses he has waited decades, grieving. Emotional beat: guilt, loyalty, and the weight of an oath kept too long.

chapters.title: The Tithe-Collector's Mark
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The collector finds her again and brands her hand with the court's mark—now the mountain can see her wherever she goes. A dying stag gives her shelter and a warning: the thirteenth moon opens a door that works both ways. Emotional beat: hunted, exposed, but more determined.

chapters.title: Company of the Kindly Ones
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She takes refuge with a hidden community of gifted outcasts who survive by masking their magic as mundane craft. Their leader, a blind weaver, reads the ledger and reveals the original bargain bought the valley's silence—her family's safety was purchased with Tam's soul before he was born. Emotional beat: fury at inherited sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Did Not Say
chapters.summary: The weaver's POV. The weaver remembers Odile's grandmother as a girl who fled the court with a stolen soul-token, which is why the debt fell to her descendants. She gives Odile a woven map to the mountain's under-roads and a hard truth: the court may simply refuse to trade. Emotional beat: inherited courage, inherited sin.

chapters.title: Under the Mountain's Root
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Ashen enter the under-roads, navigating passages that rearrange when unobserved. She uses her gift to bargain with stone-moles and blind bats, mapping a path by beast-speech. The mark on her hand burns hotter with every step. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage, the gift fully come into its own.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reaches the court: a cathedral of bone and moonlight where the old gods sit as a quarreling parliament, sustained by prayers and souls. She sees Tam, hollow and silver-eyed, serving wine to gods. She must not reveal herself before she understands the rules. Emotional beat: awe curdled into horror.

chapters.title: A Seat at the Parliament of Gods
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, disguised as a soul-servant. She learns the court's law: any debt may be renegotiated before witnesses if a greater price is offered, but the gods may take the offerer instead. The Debt-God, who first answered her prayer in the valley, recognizes her and says nothing. Emotional beat: terror threaded with the first glimmer of a plan.

chapters.title: The Debt-God's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Debt-God privately reveals the truth: the original prayer was her grandmother's plea for the valley's protection, and the court has been starving since the old prayers stopped. He offers Odile a trade—Tam's freedom for her memories of Tam, which the starving gods will consume as worship. Emotional beat: the trap of a fair-seeming price.

chapters.title: What Odile Would Forget
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile rehearses her memories of Tam to decide what she can bear to lose, and discovers the gods want not just memories but the love in them—the only nourishment left. Ashen argues for a different path: his centuries of remembered devotion to her grandmother. Emotional beat: love measured in what it costs to keep it.

chapters.title: Before the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. Ashen petitions the parliament to substitute his hoarded centuries of loyalty for Odile's memories, invoking the original bargain's witness-clause. The gods deliberate; the Debt-God argues for Odile's offer, hungry for fresher love. The moon begins to rise. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered quietly, without asking permission.

chapters.title: The Parliament of the Hungry Gods
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The court convenes to judge both offers. Odile, refusing to let Ashen pay alone, offers a third thing: not a memory but a promise—to carry the old gods' names back into the world and teach the valley to pray again, feeding them with living worship instead of devoured souls. Emotional beat: the climax of wit and heart over mere payment.

chapters.title: The Door of the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The gods accept, but the Debt-God demands a surety: Ashen's centuries as collateral until the first new prayer is spoken. As the thirteenth moon opens the door, Odile takes Tam's hand and leads him out while the court's light dims behind them. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by what was left behind.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Home
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, slowly re-becoming himself, remembers fragments of his hollow servitude and his sister's voice calling him back. They travel home through the burnt country, Odile now marked, gifted, and unable to hide. Emotional beat: fragile recovery, siblings relearning each other.

chapters.title: The First New Prayer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the valley stones, Odile speaks the first open prayer in a generation, and the Debt-God releases Ashen's centuries—but the wolf, emptied of his long memory, chooses to remain as an ordinary wolf at her side. The valley's magic-dead silence breaks; small wonders begin. Emotional beat: grief and grace braided together.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Crown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Epilogue a season later: Odile teaches valley children the names of the small gods, Tam plants the fields with whispered blessings, and the ledger is rewritten with the debt marked paid. The final page reveals her grandmother's true name was Beatrix, and the 'crown' was the burden she carried. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—truth chosen over invisibility, at last.
